title: Flapjacks
subtitle: Golden syrup and oat traybake
excerpt: Rolled oats bound with butter, golden syrup, and brown sugar, pressed into a tin and baked until golden. Chewy in the centre, crisp at the edges, and deeply satisfying.

recipe.sourceNotes: Flapjacks are a distinctly British bake with no direct equivalent in other countries. The word 'flapjack' in American English refers to a pancake; in Britain it means these golden-syrup-and-oat traybake bars. The recipe is extremely simple: oats, butter, golden syrup, and sugar are the only essential ingredients. The ratio of ingredients determines the texture: more golden syrup and less flour-like binding gives a chewier flapjack; more baking at a higher temperature gives a crispier one. Golden syrup, a British invert sugar syrup made from refined sugarcane, is the defining flavour. There is no close substitute for it. Flapjacks keep well in an airtight tin for up to a week and travel extremely well, making them the ideal picnic and packed-lunch bake.

recipeTools.notes: A 20 x 30 cm shallow baking tin, lined.

content.text: The mixture will look loose when it goes into the tin. Press it down firmly and evenly with the back of a spoon or a palette knife. Score into bars as soon as it comes out of the oven, while it is still soft: this makes cutting clean portions much easier once it has cooled and hardened. Do not cut through completely until fully cooled.
Heat the oven to 180 C / fan 160 C / gas 4. Line a 20 x 30 cm tin with baking paper. Melt the butter, golden syrup, sugar, and salt together in a large saucepan over low heat, stirring until smooth.
Remove from the heat. Stir in the rolled oats until every oat is coated. Tip into the prepared tin and press firmly into an even layer.

Bake for 20 to 25 minutes until deep golden at the edges and just set in the centre. Immediately score into 16 bars with a sharp knife, cutting about halfway through. Leave to cool completely in the tin before turning out and cutting through fully.
